Date 30 Dec 1930

Subject (in full) Chang Ching Mou 張敬

Made by Supt Tan Shao Liang Forwarded by Tho Robertson, Supt.

Chang Ching Mou 張敬謨 is not known to military
officers who are natives of Hupeh. There is no person
bearing this name who lives or visits 447 Yong Ho Lee 永和里
North Thibet Road. Discreet enquiries show that one
Chang Shao Wen 張少文 about 25 years of age native of Yi Cheng
Kompo frequents this address. He is most probably the man
referred to. This man claims to be attached to a
military office in Nanking.
However, careful enquiries have elicited the information
that he was at one time employed as 4th Class Clerk at Harbin
Road Station but his services were terminated on 30.8.30
owing, I understand, to unsatisfactory work. He is being
supported by Koc Sz 顧四 alias Koc Tso Hsien 顧左賢 alias
Koc Mou Su 顧茂如 the occupant of 447 North Thibet Road, who
is said to be on terms of intimacy with his (Chang's) sister.
Chang is said to be associated with loafers and opium smugglers.
Koo Sz, the occupant of 447 N. Thibet Road is a Paung leader
with several thousand followers mostly of questionable characters.
Beginning as a ricsha coolie he came to Shanghai about 30 years
ago from Yi Cheng (North of Yangtse). He joined the S.M.P.
as a C.D.C. and was stationed at Louza. After he had been
dismissed or told to resign, he kept a teashop called Teh Sheng
Ler in Sungkiang Road Chapel but this was closed after 2 years.
He then opened a theatre in Mongolia Road Chapei. The
business failed and later he started another teashop called
Peh Lo in Chapei and at the same time ran a ricsha hong.
This was in 1913 Subsequently he joined the Chapei Volunteer
Corps as a Chief Detective from which he made a little fortune.
Eventually he raised shares and bought over the Tien Shien

特别分部警署，
日期 1930年12月30日

事由（全称） 张敬謨 (Chang Ching Mou)

由谭绍良 (Tan Shao Liang) 警司制作 经罗伯逊 (Tho Robertson) 警司转呈

据湖北籍军官所知，并无名为张敬謨 (Chang Ching Mou) 之人。在西藏北路447号永和里 (Yong Ho Lee)，亦无居住或来访此名者。经审慎查询，一名约25岁、籍贯宜城 (Yi Cheng) 的张少文 (Chang Shao Wen) 经常出入该地址。此人极有可能是所指对象。此人声称隶属于南京某军事机构。
然而，经仔细查询获悉，他曾任哈尔滨路警署四等书记员，但因工作表现不佳，于1930年8月30日被解职。据我了解，他的生活费用由西藏北路447号的住户顾四 (Koc Sz)，又名顾左贤 (Koc Tso Hsien)，又名顾茂如 (Koc Mou Su) 资助，据说顾与张的妹妹关系亲密。据说张与游手好闲之徒及鸦片走私犯有牵连。
西藏北路447号的住户顾四 (Koo Sz) 是一名帮会头目，拥有数千名追随者，其中大多品行可疑。他起初是一名黄包车夫，约30年前从长江以北的宜城 (Yi Cheng) 来到上海。他曾作为华籍侦探 (C.D.C.) 加入上海公共租界工部局警务处 (S.M.P.)，并被派往老闸捕房。在他被开除或被迫辞职后，他在松江路教堂附近经营一家名为德盛乐 (Teh Sheng Ler) 的茶馆，但两年后关闭。随后，他在闸北蒙古路开设了一家戏院。生意失败后，他又在闸北开设了一家名为百乐 (Peh Lo) 的茶馆，同时经营一家黄包车行。那是1913年的事。此后，他加入闸北义勇队担任首席侦探，并由此发了一笔小财。最终，他募集股份，收购了九江路上的天蟾舞台 (Tien Shien Wo Tae theatre)，演员张藏中恒 (Chang Zang Chung Heng) 是股东之一。两人发生争执，张藏离开该剧团，加入了福州路的天一舞台 (Tih Yi Tae theatre)。不久后，张藏在福州路戏院外被暗杀，顾四 (Koo Sx) 因此案被捕，但因证据不足获释。
顾四作为一名帮会头目，像其他头目一样，正积极扩展其影响力并网罗追随者。毫无疑问，当追随者向他求助时，他经常干预涉及其追随者的刑事或民事案件。例如，宋国槐 (Sung Kuo Wei) 是一名前政府代理人，也是顾的追随者，因法租界的一起绑架案在顾位于湖北路的寓所被捕，当时另有三名同伙已在押。通过顾的干预，那三人被判处五年徒刑并驱逐出境，而他的追随者宋则被判处四年徒刑但不驱逐出境，从而使其能够逃避要求引渡他的中国当局的惩罚。为了将其影响力扩展到法租界，顾最近已成为黄庆荣 (Hwang Ching Yung) 的追随者。

Wo Tae theatre on Kiukiang Road of which Chang Zang Chung
Heng an actor was one of the shareholders. The two men had
a quarrel and Zang left the establishment and joined the
Tih Yi Tae theatre on Foochow Road. Zang was assassinated
outside the Foochow Road theatre shortly afterwards
and Koo Sx was arrested in connection with the case
but was released on ground of unsufficient evidence.
Koo being a Paung leader is, like other leaders, engaged in
actively extending his influence and gathering followers.
There is no doubt that he has frequently interfered in
criminal or civil cases in which his followers are involved
when they call upon him for assistance. For instance
one Sung Kuo Wei 宋国槐 ex Government agent who is a
follower of Koo, was arrested at the latter's house in
Hupeh Road in connection with a kidnapping case in the
French Concession where three other associates were already
in custody. Through the interference of Koo, the three men
were sentenced to 5 years and expulsion but Sung his follower
was sentenced to 4 years without expulsion, thus to enable
him to evade punishment by the Chinese Authorities who
applied for his extradition. To extend his influence to
the French Concession Koo has recently become a follower
of Hwang Ching Yung.

Superintendent.

D.C. (Cr & Sp. Br's)

December 19, 1930.

Superintendent Tan.

Please make discreet and exhaustive enquiries
into the antecedents of one Chang Ching-mon (張敬謨),
native of Hupeh and ex-Army Officer, who gives his
address as c/o 447 Yoong Ho Lee ( 永□里 ), North
Thibet Road.
Your report should ■ include full particulars
of his connection with this address together with
minute details of the antecedents and activities of
the occupant or occupants of 447 Yoong Ho Lee.

O. C. Special Branch.

Date December 15, 1930.

Subject (in full) Further report on attached application

Made by ______ and ______ Forwarded by C.D.I. Hunter

Sir,

Further with reference to attached application.
Mr Gilmore, No 20 Minghong Road, American Church Mission, states
that he does not know the applicant personally, and that Mr
Ancell who gave Chang Ching Mou (張敬謀) the attached letter
of recommendation was only in Shanghai for a few days in
October 1930 when he wrote the letter. Mr Ancell is attached
to the Mission, Yangchow Branch, and very seldom comes to Shang-
hai except on business and then only for a few days.
Mr Davidson referred to in the applicant's letter dated October
24, 1930, has left China for good.

I understand that the applicant's military papers
have been handed over to Det. Supt. Gilbert.

Further verification with regards to the appli-
cant's antecedents cannot be obtained unless a letter is writ-
ten to Mr B. L. Ancell, M.A., Principal of the Mahan School,
Yangchow.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently

C.D.I.

Date December 1st 1930

Subject (in full) Report on attached application.

Made By _______ Forwarded by C.D.I. Hunter

Sir,
I beg to report that the applicant Tsang Ching Mou
(張敬謀), age 24, native of Wuchang, in the province of Hupeh.
At the age of 22 he joined the Army under General Chiang Kai
Shek (蔣介石), serving for one year and rising to the rank of
Captain. He resigned after one year's service at the request
of his parents and returned to Shanghai in May 1929, where he
again took up his studies. Prior to joining the Army he re-
sided in Shanghai for some time, he was educated at the
Nanking University for two years but had to finish before he
graduated therefore received no certificates.
The applicant is a man of very smart appearance, well-
educated, speaks English very good, and after a few month's
training, he would probably make a very good Detective. He is
one of the most likely candidates for the Crime Branch I have
interviewed lately.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently,
J. Hunter
C.D.I.

先生，
谨报告，申请人张敬謀 (Tsang Ching Mou)，24岁，籍贯湖北省武昌。
22岁时，他加入蒋介石 (Chiang Kai Shek) 将军麾下军队，服役一年并晋升至上尉军衔。应父母要求，他在服役一年后辞职，于1929年5月返回上海，重新求学。在参军之前，他曾在上海居住一段时间，曾在南京大学就读两年，但未毕业即离校，因此未获得任何证书。
申请人外表精明，受过良好教育，英语说得很好，经过几个月的训练，他可能会成为一名非常优秀的侦探。他是我近期面试过的刑事分部候选人中最有希望的一位。

此致
敬礼，
J. 亨特
C.D.I.

October, 1st 1936.

Mr. R. C. Lucas,
A. C. (C. B.)
S. M. C.

Dear Sir:

I respectfully submit the following information for the
purpose of applying a position in your Branch as a C. D. C. First
I know you will be surprised that how can I be a detective as I am
not an uniformed police. For detective has to be trained from the young
otherwise how can he become it. But I am different with some others
for I have been with the detective branch about two years; how to arrest
the robbers, how to discover the property, how to investigate and how
to discriminate it is true. And I also accept all the regulations
of Shanghai Municipal Police.

Hoping to better myself, and believing that I have the qualifications
to serve you, I take the opportunity to enclose the application.
I am a native of Suchang, Hup., aged □□, married, and in excellent
health. After I graduated from Makon School, Yangchow, I continued my
study at the University of Nanking. After two years' study, I left there
due to the financial difficulties, and thus my school life was brought
to an end. For I like to do something useful, so I entered the Chinese
Customs office. Not very long I resigned from my post to let them
admit me again.

I have a fair knowledge of English and Chinese, and also I
can speak both of local as well as Peking dialect.

As to my standing and personality, I refer you to Mr. B. J. Thomas,
the principal of Makon School, or to Mr. J. F. Davidson, professor of
page_data.zh:
1936年10月1日。

R. C. 卢卡斯 (Lucas) 先生，
助理总监 (刑事分部)
上海公共租界工部局。

尊敬的先生：

谨提交以下信息，以申请贵分部华籍侦探 (C. D. C.) 职位。首先，我知道您会惊讶于我并非制服警察如何能成为一名侦探。因为侦探必须从小接受训练，否则怎能胜任。但我与其他人不同，因为我已在侦探分部工作约两年；懂得如何逮捕强盗，如何查获赃物，如何调查以及如何辨别真伪。我也遵守上海公共租界工部局警务处的所有规章。

希望提升自我，并相信我有资格为您效劳，借此机会附上申请。我籍贯江苏苏州 (Suchang, Hup.)，年龄□□，已婚，身体健康。从扬州马康学校 (Makon School) 毕业后，我继续在南京大学求学。学习两年后，因经济困难离校， thus 我的学生生涯就此结束。因为我想做些有益的事，所以我进入了中国海关办公室。不久后我辞职，以便让他们再次录用我。（注：此处原文逻辑似有误，照实翻译）

我具备良好的中英文知识，也能说本地话和北京话。

关于我的地位和人品，我可向您推荐马康学校校长 B. J. 托马斯 (Thomas) 先生，或圣约翰大学的 J. F. 戴维森 (Davidson) 教授，

I am, Dear Sir,

Chang Ching Man

page_data.en:
Translation of the attached letter of appointment.

July 23, (?).

Comrade Tsang Chao-wan.

This is to inform you that according to a
verbal instruction from our Chief you have been appointed
member of the Political Training Section of the 279th
Regiment, concurrently acting as Secretary to Lieutenant
Hang.

General Office of the Political Training
Section of the 92nd Division of the 31st Army
of the National Troops.

Translation of the attached notice of appointment.

September 1, 1927.

Tsang Chao-wan alias Tsang Ching-moo is appointed
a member of the Telegram Office attached to the Staff Office
of this Army.

Brigadier Commander Tsang Chung-li
D/Brigadier Commander Tsang Tung.
92nd Division of the 31st Army of
the National Revolutionary Troops.

7月23日，(?)。

张兆万 (Tsang Chao-wan) 同志。

兹通知你，根据我们主任的口头指示，你已被任命为第279团政治训练处成员，兼任杭 (Hang) 中尉秘书。

国民革命军第三十一军第九十二师
政治训练处总办公室。

所附委任通知的译文。

1927年9月1日。

张兆万，又名张敬謨 (Tsang Ching-moo)，被任命为本军参谋处附属电报处成员。

旅长 张忠立 (Tsang Chung-li)
代旅长 张东 (Tsang Tung)。
国民革命军第三十一军
第九十二师。
